ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the given figure, within $\triangle ABC$, $AD \perp BC$, $AE$ is the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$. If $\angle B = 72^\circ$ and $\angle C = 38^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=72^\circ$ and $\angle C=38^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=180^\circ-72^\circ-38^\circ=70^\circ$,\\
since $AD\perp BC$,\\
thus $\angle ADC=90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle DAC=90^\circ-\angle C=90^\circ-38^\circ=52^\circ$;\\
since $AE$ bisects $\angle BAC$,\\
thus $\angle EAC= \frac{1}{2}\angle BAC=35^\circ$;\\
therefore $\angle DAE=\angle DAC-\angle EAC=52^\circ-35^\circ=\boxed{17^\circ}$.

Then reason: It is known that ∠B = 72°, ∠C = 38°, so the sum of the interior angles of the triangle gives ∠BAC = 180° − 72° − 38° = 70°. Because AD is perpendicular to BC, in right triangle ADC, ∠DAC = 90° − ∠C = 90° − 38° = 52°. Because AE is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, ∠EAC = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°. In the figure AE is between AD and AC, therefore ∠DAE = ∠DAC − ∠EAC = 52° − 35° = 17°.
